item.title: Nvidia publishes report on open AI model weights and their impact on American AI leadership
item.description: Nvidia released a report discussing the role of open AI model weights in maintaining and advancing American leadership in artificial intelligence. The document explores how openness in AI model sharing can influence innovation and competitiveness in the AI sector. The report provides analysis on the strategic importance of accessible AI resources for research and development within the United States.

item.title: BFL.ai launches FLUX 3 multimodal foundation model for joint image, video, and audio understanding and generation, now in Early Access [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: BFL.ai has released FLUX 3, a new multimodal foundation model designed to learn from images, videos, and audio simultaneously within a unified architecture. The model aims to capture a comprehensive representation of the world by integrating spatial, temporal, and acoustic information, enabling it to perceive, predict, and act across physical and digital environments. FLUX 3 supports diverse capabilities including text-to-video generation with audio up to 20 seconds, image-to-video generation, video-to-video transformation, and multilingual dialogue. Early evaluations show FLUX 3 outperforming several existing models in video generation quality and style diversity. The model is currently available in Early Access, with ongoing development expected to improve its performance further.

item.title: Black Forest Labs and mimic launch FLUX-mimic, a next-generation video-action model for robot manipulation based on the multimodal FLUX 3 foundation model [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Black Forest Labs (BFL) and mimic have developed FLUX-mimic, a video-action model built on the FLUX 3 multimodal foundation model that jointly generates images, video, audio, and robot actions. FLUX 3 was trained to understand physical world dynamics through video prediction, enabling it to model cause and effect, motion, and contact, which supports both content creation and robotic manipulation. FLUX-mimic integrates BFL's visual foundation model expertise with mimic's robotics and deployment capabilities, resulting in a model tested and deployed on real production lines, including at Audi. The model's single backbone architecture allows it to predict robot actions without sacrificing video generation quality, demonstrating that physical AI and content creation can share a unified underlying model of the world.

item.title: Anthropic publishes Claude Cookbook with detailed guides for building and deploying AI agents using Claude Managed Agents API [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Anthropic has released the Claude Cookbook, a comprehensive resource offering tutorials and examples for developing AI agents with the Claude Managed Agents API. The cookbook covers a wide range of use cases including multi-agent coordination, safety fallback mechanisms, memory stores, vulnerability discovery, incident response, and integration with external tools and workflows. The resource provides step-by-step instructions for deploying agents across different environments such as Docker and Kubernetes, managing session memory and prompt versioning, and building specialized applications like voice assistants, financial dashboards, and research agents. It aims to help developers scale and optimize Claude-based AI applications with practical code samples and operational best practices.

item.title: Echo system combines open-weight models to match Fable-level AI results at one third the inference cost [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Echo is a new AI system that dynamically allocates computation across multiple open-weight models to optimize performance for each request. It selects which models to use and how to combine their outputs, achieving results comparable to the stronger Fable system but at roughly one third of the inference cost. The developer found that even weaker models can contribute effectively in combination, improving overall accuracy beyond any single model in the pool. Echo offers a chat interface and an OpenAI-compatible API for external testing. The creator is investigating cases where Echo's allocation decisions are suboptimal and exploring its application to coding and agentic tasks where quality measurement is more challenging.

item.title: Developer argues that over-constraining AI prompts limits code generation quality and advocates for simpler workflows that let AI handle coding tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A developer critiques elaborate workflows for AI-assisted code writing, stating that excessive constraints in prompts narrow the model's effectiveness and lead to subpar results. They suggest a simpler two-step approach where the AI is first given relevant context and then instructed on what to build, allowing the model to naturally follow conventions and patterns without micromanagement. The article highlights that developers often resist fully trusting AI because it challenges their traditional sense of control and value tied to coding output. Instead of adding complex layers of oversight, the author encourages embracing AI's capabilities and focusing on higher-level tasks like choosing the technology stack and monitoring AI output quality, while avoiding unnecessary procedural overhead.

item.title: Jensen Huang says NVIDIA supports open AI models to enhance safety, innovation, and US AI leadership [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang shared a letter emphasizing the importance of open AI models for transforming industries, enhancing cybersecurity, accelerating innovation, and supporting national sovereignty. He stated that both closed and open frontier AI models are necessary for global progress. Huang's message highlights NVIDIA's commitment to fostering an open AI ecosystem to maintain American leadership in artificial intelligence.

item.title: Hacker News user asks if there can be a day without AI news coverage
item.description: A user on Hacker News raised a question about the possibility of having a day free from AI-related news. The discussion reflects ongoing interest and perhaps fatigue regarding the constant flow of AI news in technology communities.

item.title: Fly.io refocuses on Sprites, specialized computers for AI agents, with new funding and leadership changes [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Fly.io announced a strategic shift to concentrate on Sprites, their specialized computers designed to support AI agents, accompanied by new funding and the appointment of Scott Johnston as CEO. The company aims to address the evolving needs of AI-driven software development by providing infrastructure tailored for adaptive, agent-based applications. This move reflects Fly.io's recognition of the changing landscape in cloud infrastructure, where traditional models are less suited for AI agents that require explicit, flexible deployment environments. The company plans to leverage its platform to enable easier and more efficient deployment of AI-powered applications, anticipating a future where personalized and adaptive software becomes the norm.

item.title: Bluesky expands AI assistant Attie into an open social research tool with new Quests feature for AT Protocol apps [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Bluesky has enhanced its AI assistant Attie with a new feature called Quests, enabling users to ask open-ended questions about news, trends, and conversations across the Bluesky social network and other apps using the AT Protocol. This expansion aims to help users research and make sense of information on the open social web, addressing misinformation and noise. Attie, launched in March, originally allowed users to build custom social feeds without programming. The new capabilities let users identify trending topics and influential accounts, with the company planning further accessibility improvements and a redesigned interface. The feature is currently in beta, with users invited from a waitlist over the coming weeks as Bluesky seeks to grow its user base and explore monetization options amid slowing growth.

item.title: Midjourney acquires astrology app Co-Star with 4.3 million monthly users, expanding beyond image and video AI [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Midjourney, known for its AI-powered image and video generation, has acquired Co-Star, a social astrology app with about 4.3 million monthly active users. The acquisition brings Co-Star's team of around two dozen employees into Midjourney as it broadens its product offerings beyond its core AI tools. Co-Star combines AI and human input to generate horoscopes, compatibility assessments, and personalized astrological advice that users can share socially. Midjourney's move may signal plans to develop a standalone app leveraging Co-Star's consumer experience, complementing its existing AI services and medical initiatives.

item.title: Report: AI coding tools may hinder skill development by removing necessary learning friction, creating challenges for novice developers to gain expertise [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The article argues that while AI coding assistants offer benefits, they may prevent deep skill formation by eliminating the challenges that foster expertise. Novice developers relying heavily on AI risk developing an illusion of competence without true understanding, as these tools require expert-level skills to use effectively. A study by JetBrains found that developers who limited AI assistance performed better by maintaining critical problem-solving steps and developing the ability to discern helpful AI suggestions. This dynamic creates a paradox where AI tools demand expertise to be used well but also reduce opportunities to acquire that expertise, potentially impacting the long-term development of programming skills.

item.title: Silicon Valley splits over Chinese open-weight AI models amid concerns of IP theft and security risks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Silicon Valley is deeply divided over the rise of Chinese open-weight AI models, with major AI companies like Anthropic raising alarms about intellectual property theft and security risks, while smaller startups oppose US government restrictions. The debate centers on the rapid spread of these models, which lack the safety guardrails of proprietary systems but enable faster innovation and broader access. Anthropic has accused Chinese firms Alibaba and Moonshot AI of illicitly using its technology through distillation attacks, prompting concerns in Washington and the Valley. Meanwhile, a coalition of over 200 startups, including YCombinator, has lobbied against banning open-weight models, arguing that such restrictions would stifle competition and favor large AI giants. Investors like Bill Gurley emphasize the importance of open models for startup growth, while critics warn of potential security vulnerabilities. The controversy highlights a tension between protecting proprietary AI advancements and fostering an open ecosystem that benefits smaller players and innovation. US policymakers face challenges balancing national security, economic interests, and the future of AI development amid this complex landscape.

item.title: Trump administration launches $5 billion Genesis Mission grants for AI-driven science projects, aiming to reshape US research priorities [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: The Trump administration announced the first Genesis Mission grants, allocating $5 billion to support hundreds of AI-driven science projects across fields like drug discovery, energy, and robotics. The initiative is described by the White House as comparable in urgency to the Manhattan Project and aims to accelerate scientific discovery by leveraging artificial intelligence. The program reflects a broader shift in US science policy under Trump, emphasizing AI, robotics, and nuclear energy while reducing focus on life sciences. It also signals a move toward prioritizing individual researchers and private companies over traditional academic institutions, with political appointees gaining more control over federal funding decisions. Critics warn this approach treats science like a startup, potentially undermining the slow, uncertain nature of basic research that has historically driven major discoveries.

item.title: OpenAI adds ChatGPT Voice to desktop app, enabling voice control of AI agents and complex tasks with ChatGPT Work and Codex [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has updated its ChatGPT desktop app to include ChatGPT Voice, a feature that allows users to interact with the app using voice commands to control AI agents and perform multi-step tasks. This update leverages OpenAI's GPT-Live voice models and supports integration with ChatGPT Work and Codex, enabling users to dictate complex commands and respond interactively within the app. The desktop version enhances capabilities beyond the smartphone release by allowing control over computer functions, including accessing websites and apps, and on macOS, using Appshots to read screen content. OpenAI demonstrated the feature handling developer tasks such as creating threads and pull requests with a single voice command. Users can also access ChatGPT Voice in Codex remotely via the iOS app.

item.title: Developer reflects on AI-assisted coding evolution from skepticism to productivity gains with tools like GitHub Copilot and Claude [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A developer recounts their journey from skepticism to embracing AI-assisted coding tools such as GitHub Copilot and Claude, which have significantly accelerated their programming workflow. They describe how AI has evolved to write code blocks and functions, enhancing productivity beyond traditional IDE auto-completion. The developer also shares their experience with vintage computing projects on classic Macintosh systems, highlighting the contrast between manual coding and AI-generated software. They note a shift in the community's perception, where AI-generated projects have become common, sometimes diminishing enthusiasm for new software developments. Despite this, the developer acknowledges the practical benefits of AI while maintaining a critical perspective on the broader AI industry and its surrounding hype.

item.title: AI industry urges US policymakers to avoid broad restrictions on open-weight models amid concerns over Chinese AI advancements [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Several AI companies including Hugging Face, Meta, Microsoft, Mistral, and Nvidia have signed an open letter urging US policymakers not to impose broad restrictions on open-weight AI models. The letter warns against conflating legitimate techniques like model distillation with intellectual property theft and emphasizes the importance of openness for innovation and cybersecurity defense. The letter comes as the US government debates responses to allegations of Chinese AI labs stealing intellectual property and growing in capability, with some reports suggesting potential bans on Chinese open-weight models. Signatories argue that targeted legal frameworks should address unlawful activities rather than sweeping restrictions that could hinder AI development and defensive capabilities.

The letter was issued as the Trump administration considers imposing restrictions on Chinese AI labs, highlighting concerns over potential regulatory impacts on AI development and collaboration.

item.title: Sakana updates Fugu Ultra AI router to v1.1, claims it outperforms Fable 5 without including it in the model pool [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Sakana AI has released version 1.1 of its Fugu Ultra AI router, claiming performance improvements of up to 7.9 points over the previous version and asserting it now outperforms Fable 5 despite not including Fable 5 in its model selection pool. These claims are based on Sakana's own evaluations, with no independent verification available yet. The update adds a Claude Code-compatible endpoint and maintains pricing at $5 per million input tokens and $30 per million output tokens. Fugu Ultra remains unavailable in the EU due to GDPR and regional regulations. Since its initial release, the router has been accessible on platforms like OpenRouter and Vercel, though earlier versions received mixed reviews for token usage, speed, and results.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Health feature to integrate Apple Health data and US medical records for users aged 18 and older across web and iOS [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced a Health feature within ChatGPT that allows users aged 18 and older to connect their Apple Health data and, where supported, medical records from US hospital systems, One Medical, or Function Health. This integration enables ChatGPT to access medications, lab results, recent visits, sleep data, and activity logs during conversations, enhancing personalized responses without requiring users to enter a dedicated health mode. The feature is available across Free, Go, Plus, and Pro tiers on web and iOS. Early testers reported benefits such as clearer understanding of medical histories, longitudinal health pattern analysis, and improved communication with healthcare providers. OpenAI emphasizes that the tool is designed to support users in managing their health information rather than providing clinical diagnoses, with the Health tab serving as a management hub for connected accounts and data review.

item.title: Nvidia Shares Are Priced For Everything To Go Wrong: That Makes No Sense
item.description: Shares of Nvidia don't trade like those of a company whose revenues are expected to rise 83% this year. Instead, the stock is priced as though everything that could go wrong in the next couple of years will go wrong. That creates an opportunity for investors willing to take a longer view. Most semiconductor investors are chasing the stocks they think will grow the fastest over the next few years. So while shares of Nvidia have appreciated just 10% so far this year, distant rival Advanced Micro Devices is up 142%, while memory chip maker Micron, whose business has exploded thanks to demand from AI data centers, is up 213% year to date. The Philadelphia semiconductor index is up 71%.

item.description: The British AI Security Institute and the U.S. Center for AI Standards and Innovation tested Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 on offensive cyber tasks. Kimi K3 scored 32 percent on ExploitBench, compared with 76 percent for leading U.S. models, while its safeguards failed to block exploit development or simulated attacks. The gap between its strong general benchmark scores and weaker cyber performance also fits allegations that Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic's models. item.title: Wall Street Sends Google a Message [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Maybe, just maybe, big tech firms need to do a better job of explaining their AI investment strategies. Shares of Google parent Alphabet fell 7% on Thursday after the company disclosed a further increase in capital expenditures this year-money it will spend on new AI chips, servers and data centers. The drop all but wiped out the gains the stock had enjoyed so far this year. Sure, the entire stock market sold off, presumably as a result of rising oil prices and the intensification of the Iran war. But Alphabet was among the worst hit, along with Tesla, which also reported sharply higher capex on Wednesday and whose shares fell 15% on Thursday. It's tough to consider Tesla's stock valuation on any kind of rational basis, given that it trades based more on its connection to Elon Musk than reality. But Alphabet is a different animal.

item.title: The Startups Angling to Go Public After Anthropic [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Before we get into today's column, some breaking news: Stripe is in talks to buy OpenRouter for about $10 billion. The news follows our report Friday that the $1.3 billion-valuation startup, which helps companies choose the best and cheapest AI models, was the target of takeover interest. Databricks was also in early discussions to buy the startup, we reported today. For more on why Stripe can make big acquisitions, read our exclusive reporting on its financials here. Mutual funds and other large investors considering buying into Anthropic's initial public offering are slated to meet with the AI company over the next several days. Along with Anthropic's plans to secure compute and the rise of Chinese models, big investors are likely to have questions about the structure of the IPO-including when shareholders can sell. The potential for Anthropic to dump the typical IPO playbook was raised in a scoop by Cory earlier today. Anthropic is considering requiring rank-and-file employees-rather than just top executives-to sell stock through rigid trading schedules. It's not just the investors who will be closely following Anthropic's IPO moves. Startups are keeping an eye on the listing, which could happen as soon as September, as they consider their own public plans. No one wants to compete with Anthropic for investors' attention. But if it goes well, it could unlock a wave of IPOs from other tech startups, particularly those riding the groundswell of consumer and business interest in AI-as well as others that argue they're immune from AI-generated volatility.

item.title: Sierra Acquires Agent Startup 'Takeoff' to Diversify Its Business [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: In 2020, 22-year-old Aakash Thumaty was a product manager at Salesforce when he wrote an essay, "Value Driven Innovation at Shopify and the Incumbency Trap at Salesforce," which argued against Salesforce's subscription-based business model. He sent it to Bret Taylor, who at the time was Salesforce's chief operating officer. To Thumaty's surprise, Taylor shared it with other executives at the company. Six years later, Thumaty and Taylor's paths are crossing again. Sierra, the AI customer support startup Taylor now leads, is acquiring Thumaty's three-person startup, Takeoff, which develops agents that can work on tasks for long periods of time, the companies told The Information exclusively. They wouldn't disclose details but it's unlikely to have been a high priced acquisition. Takeoff was founded a year ago and was closing in on $10 million in annualized revenue earlier this month, Thumaty said. (It had previously raised $15 million in funding from Matrix and venture capitalist Lachy Groom.) But Sierra executives hope Thumaty's expertise will come in handy as the company tries to move beyond AI-powered customer support agents into selling agents for other tasks.

item.title: Anthropic Considers Unusual Plan for Employee Stock Sales After It Goes Public
item.description: As Anthropic prepares to go public, it is considering a highly unusual move to require rank-and-file employees to sell stock through rigid trading schedules so they don't run afoul of insider trading laws, said a person familiar with the matter and a person briefed on it. At companies that have used such trading plans, typically only top executives and some finance and legal staff adopt them. The arrangements, called 10b5-1 plans, require executives and directors to sell stock according to preset schedules that outline how many shares they'll sell and at what prices.
